I'm not a specialist in journalism or anything, but I am old enough to remember life before 24 hour news networks. Here are my two cents.

Way back when TV and radio were first becoming ubiquitous the federal government created the FCC. The FCC allowed certain radio frequencies to be used for commercial purposes (TV and radio stations usually) so long as they set aside an hour every day for use as an unbiased news source. I know that being completely unbiased isn't possible, but these guys (and some gals by the end of it) were very professional and did a great job of keeping their bias to a minimum.

In the early 90's the first 24 hour news network came into being. Everyone thought it was a pants on head retarded idea, and the station was doomed to fail. Then Desert Storm happened. After that Clinton (Bill) started jizzing on interns. After that the ratings soared, and the board of directors started putting pressure on sensationalizing everything since it made money, and since these were cable networks and not coming in over the radio waves (controlled by the FCC) they had no legal requirement to be ethical in their journalism. There was still pressure from the old guard (people like Dan Rather), but they are all retired now and any pretense of neutrality or honesty has flown out the window.

On the other hand you have people like Lenny Bruce, or George Carlin telling you that the whole world is fucked and that there is nothing you can do about it. They've been telling you this the entire time, and for the most part they are still telling us this (even when their politics don't line up with ours, the message is almost always the world is fucked. It's just he here's why that is different).
